label: On-premises
description: A site's own infrastructure: networks and VLANs, firewalls, routers, servers, server clusters, load balancers and database servers.

types.label: Network
types.description: A site's private network (LAN). Its VLANs reach each other through the core switches unless a firewall filters them; the internet is reached through the network's firewall.

addressSpace.title: Address space
addressSpace.description: The network's IPv4 address range, for example 192.168.0.0/16. Used by the detailed analysis level.

types.label: VLAN
types.description: A segment of the network; place it in the network. A firewall can filter the traffic that enters or leaves it.

subnet.title: Subnet
subnet.description: The VLAN's IPv4 subnet within the network, for example 192.168.10.0/24. Used by the detailed analysis level.

types.label: Firewall
types.description: The network's gateway to the internet and its filter between VLANs. Hosts in the networks it connects use it as their default gateway; it translates their addresses for outbound connections and lets inbound traffic reach published servers only. Its rules apply to traffic through it and to the VLANs it protects.

networks.title: Networks
networks.description: The networks it is the internet gateway of.

protects.title: Protected VLANs
protects.description: The VLANs whose incoming and outgoing traffic it filters.

rules.title: Rules
rules.description: Checked in order; the first match decides. Without a match, inbound traffic is denied and outbound traffic is allowed. Stateful: replies are allowed automatically.

direction.title: Direction
direction.description: Seen from the protected VLAN, or from the network for traffic to and from the internet.

peer.title: Peer
peer.description: any, internet, network (anything inside the network), the id of a component, VLAN or network, or an IPv4 range such as 192.168.10.0/24 (matched at the detailed level).

ports.title: Ports
ports.description: Port ids (https), numbers (443) or ranges (8080-8090). Omitted: all ports.

locations.title: Locations
locations.description: Where its units run, such as racks or rooms; each one is a failure domain. Two units in two locations form a high-availability pair.

types.label: Router
types.description: Overrides the default gateway of the networks or VLANs it serves, for example to send internet traffic through another firewall.

routes.title: Routes
routes.description: Routes besides the network's local routes.

destination.title: Destination
destination.description: internet or an IPv4 range such as 0.0.0.0/0 (the detailed level matches the longest prefix).

serves.title: Serves
serves.description: The networks or VLANs that use it.

types.label: Server
types.description: A physical or virtual server running an application. Place it in a VLAN. A published server is reachable from the internet through the firewall.

endpoint.title: Endpoint
endpoint.description: public: published on a public address through the firewall. private: internal only.

locations.title: Locations
locations.description: Where it runs, such as a rack or a room.

types.label: Server cluster
types.description: A group of equivalent servers running an application. Place it in a VLAN; its locations say which racks, rooms or sites its servers run in.

endpoint.title: Endpoint
endpoint.description: public: published on a public address through the firewall. private: internal only.

locations.title: Locations
locations.description: Where its servers run, such as racks, rooms or sites; each one is a failure domain.

types.label: Load balancer
types.description: Distributes HTTP(S) requests to servers or clusters. Place it in a VLAN.

endpoint.title: Endpoint
endpoint.description: public: published on a public address through the firewall. private: internal only.

pools.title: Pools
pools.description: Each pool forwards requests on a path to a target.

locations.title: Locations
locations.description: Where its units run; each one is a failure domain. Two units in two locations form a high-availability pair.

types.label: Database server
types.description: A relational database server. Place it in a VLAN. Clients authenticate with database credentials, which are not modeled.

locations.title: Locations
locations.description: Where its primary and replicas run; each one is a failure domain. A replica in a second location makes it redundant.
